DECISION, explicit because the design comparison called it open: the bookend guard DOES cover retext-check. Candidate A argued the opposite (a bookend whose typo'd check can never be corrected is worse). Overridden, with the reason on the record: retext-check can rewrite a frozen gate's command check to something trivially true and then pass it, which defeats the freeze completely while leaving the gate standing — a freeze that only stops deletion is not a freeze. The typo case has a sanctioned path that does not require weakening the guard: fix the template and re-instantiate, or waive the condition with a recorded authority. Surface this to the human as a decision candidate.

Reviewer/survey is deliberately NOT in scope, and this is the reasoning rather than an omission: amend on a SURVEY already accepts a retext-check-only delta (checklist_engine.py:3013-3029), so add/drop/rescope of a survey item is structurally impossible already and a survey needs no bookend.

why_trail.why: Entering execution with the scope narrowed by the cold critic: the crew half is fenced behind scripts/generate_spine.py, which neither lane owns, so this run delivers the freeze for Admiral, Commander and Explorer and floats crew. Recording first-hand what this gate is: I am driving a SECOND checklist file under a session id I invented (commander-567-k-execute), off the door, which is exactly the defect #634 names.

The guard landed as one swappable seam, which was the requirement that mattered: _is_bookend() is the only place task.get('bookend') is read, so a future switch to a positional rule or a plan-level region is a change to one function, not a rewrite. I verified the crew rather than believing it: re-ran its tests myself (528 passed, 154 subtests, 0 FAILED) and independently reproduced all four behaviours in a fresh process against COPIES — the measured three-drop gap is now REFUSED on a declared plan, an insert past the closing bookend is REFUSED, an UNDECLARED plan still drops its closing gates exactly as at 9b38b9d9, and a refused delta leaves items untouched. The load-bearing demonstration: a Commander standing at 'plan' amended g1-implement/g1-review/g1-integrate directly into its own spine's middle, bookends frozen, with the change recorded in amendments as reason+authority+ops — #634's actual point, working, with no execute.json and no invented session id. The crew also caught an error in MY handoff: I wrote the ceiling formula as the bookend's index+1, which would have permitted the append-past-archive case my own prose said must be refused; it implemented the corrected semantics and said so.

APPROVE from an independent reviewer that reproduced rather than read: it re-ran every criterion, and on criterion 10 it broke two guards locally to confirm the new tests actually go red before restoring the tree. It also re-derived, without being told the answer, the off-by-one in candidate B's written ceiling formula that the implementer had already caught — two independent arrivals at the same defect in the design artifact, which is why I corrected DESIGN_COMPARISON.md so a later reader does not copy it. Three findings, all info/nit, none blocking: the formula divergence (a doc fix, now done), agreement rather than disagreement on covering retext-check, and a nit that the four guard messages hand-write their prose instead of sharing a builder — which I am leaving, because the messages are usefully distinct per verb and criterion 7's one-seam requirement was about the READ, not the message text.

Integrated. The c2 command postcondition ran the targeted suite itself on advance, so the close is gated on the engine's own execution, not on my report of it. The mechanism is real: a Commander at plan can now author its work gates into its own spine's middle while init and archive stay frozen, with the change legible in amendments as ts+reason+authority+ops. What is NOT yet true is that anything declares a bookend — the guard protects nothing until g2 lands the declarations in the templates, which is why g2 is not optional polish.

Six declarations landed on exactly the intended gates and no others — I verified by computing the set from the JSON myself, not by reading the diff. The diff is as small as it should be: one key appended per gate, no reformatting of files that are read constantly.

APPROVE. The reviewer did what I most wanted from criterion 7 — it judged the six choices rather than only verifying them, and it found something I had not: Admiral's closeout carries a human-acceptance postcondition baked onto the gate now frozen, while Commander's archive and Explorer's route do not, so for those two the human-confirmation requirement still lives at 'review', inside the mutable middle, and is amendable away. That means this freeze protects a run's COMPLETION but not its ACCEPTANCE. Staged as a triage candidate and deliberately not taken: baking an acceptance postcondition onto a closing bookend changes what a run must prove before it can close, which is the human's rigor-dial call and wider than #634.

Integrated. The c2 command postcondition — the one the cold critic made me add — ran on advance and asserted the exact bookend id set per template rather than trusting a reviewer's prose, which is the difference between checking the declaration landed and checking someone said it did.

Self-hosting proof and the full suite, both run in this gate rather than delegated: the whole point is that the Commander verifies its own change in its own hands, and the independent review already happened at g1 and g2 where the code was written. Read-only on both live spines exits 0 under the engine I just patched. Every mutating verb ran against copies: the exact three-drop delta that succeeded at 9b38b9d9 is now refused, the middle still grows, and a mixed delta rolls back so the legal op does not land either. The Admiral's work area is untouched.
